findings.description: If the failure happens after the tmp file was already removed or never created, or os.replace succeeded and a later step raised, `os.unlink(tmp_name)` can itself raise FileNotFoundError, masking the real error (e.g. disk full, JSON failure). The bare `except:` also catches KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit. Also, if os.fdopen itself fails, fd leaks.
findings.suggestion: Use `except BaseException:` with `try: os.unlink(tmp_name) except FileNotFoundError: pass` around the cleanup, then re-raise; or use contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError).
findings.title: Bare except cleanup can mask the original error and leave a temp file

findings.description: The previous get() deleted expired sessions lazily. The new version only returns None, so expired entries (and, in FileSessionStore, their persisted records) grow unbounded unless a caller periodically invokes purge_expired. Existing callers relying on lazy cleanup now leak memory and file size.
findings.suggestion: Either remove the expired session under the write lock in get(), or ensure purge_expired is scheduled and documented.
findings.title: Expired sessions no longer removed on get, so they accumulate until purge_expired is called
